Slice: Undelivered Notices

Step 6 of 6 in Chase an overdue loan · after My Loans — overdue notice failed · the story ends here · State View

Intent

Shows the shed manager every email the shed couldn't deliver — overdue notices and pickup notices — so they can reach the neighbor another way. A neighbor who wasn't told their loan is overdue, or that a tool is waiting for them, doesn't stay unnoticed. An entry stays only while there is something to follow up.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Undelivered Notices screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per failed overdue notice whose loan is still open, and one per failed pickup notice whose set-aside hasn't ended, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. The screen offers no actions. Following up is the shed manager's job, in person; no email is tried again after its failure is recorded (Send Overdue Notice, INV-OVN-9).
  • Which failure reports become events is decided by the two failure slices: a report that matches no notice the shed sent, or that arrives after the loan or set-aside has ended, is ignored there and never reaches this view.

Read Model / View

  • View: Undelivered Notices built from events: "Overdue Notice Failed", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Undelivered Notices screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears, changes or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes).

One row per entry. LoanId, HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
kindTextoverdue-notice or pickup-notice. Derived: from which failure event created the entry.
loanIdLoanIdOptional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.loanId.
holdIdHoldIdOptional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdThe failure event's neighborId: the borrower or the holder.
neighborNameTextThe failure event's neighborName: the name the notice was addressed to.
neighborEmailTextDerived: the failure event's neighborEmail (the address that failed), replaced by each later Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor. Always the current one.
toolIdToolIdOptional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.toolId.
toolNameTextThe failure event's toolName.
dueDateDateOptional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.dueDate, replaced by each later Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
collectByDateDateOptional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.collectByDate.
reasonTextrefused or bounced, from the failure event's reason.
failedAtInstantFrom the failure event's failedAt. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

To fill an entry the moment its failure lands, the view also keeps, for every open loan, its tool, borrower and current due date, and for every live set-aside, its tool, holder and collect-by date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry drops off.

  • An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. Retiring the tool while it is out doesn't end the loan, so the entry stays.
  • A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends: Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold. Retiring the tool or closing the holder's account ends it by recording Hold Cancelled (Retire Tool, Close Account).

Nothing brings an entry back.

Queries

  • List undelivered notices. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with all the fields above. There is no paging. Entries are listed by neighbor name, then by failedAt, the time the entry was created (INV-UDN-9).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-UDN-1: Every Overdue Notice Failed and every Pickup Notice Failed creates exactly one entry.
    • Nothing else creates an entry. A failure is recorded only after the email provider has made its 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reported a final failure, so the shed manager never sees a notice that is still being tried.
  • INV-UDN-2: Each entry shows the failure date, and whether the provider refused the email or it bounced.
    • A bounce usually means a wrong email address. The shed manager can ask the neighbor to change it from My Account.
  • INV-UDN-3: An overdue-notice entry shows the borrower's name and current email, the tool's name, and the loan's current due date.
    • The name, the email, the tool's name and the due date come with Overdue Notice Failed, the email as replaced by any later Neighbor Email Changed and the due date as moved by any later Loan Extended.
  • INV-UDN-3a: A pickup-notice entry shows the holder's name and current email, the tool's name, and the collect-by date.
    • Name, email, tool name and collect-by date come with Pickup Notice Failed; the email is replaced by any later Neighbor Email Changed.
  • INV-UDN-4: An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost.
    • Either way the loan has ended, and there is nothing left to follow up. A tool retired while out keeps its entry until one of these happens.
  • INV-UDN-5: A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside ends when the holder collects the tool, or the hold is cancelled or expires; retiring the tool or closing the holder's account records Hold Cancelled for it.
  • INV-UDN-9: Entries are listed by neighbor name, ignoring case, then by when the failure was recorded.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-UDN-8: Applying the same event twice leaves Undelivered Notices as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-UDN-10: Only the shed manager can read Undelivered Notices.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and has the cordless drill on loan L1, due 12 October. Ben Ito registered with ben@example.org, and Hold Fulfilled was recorded for his hold H1 on the hedge trimmer with a collect-by date of 16 October.

  • Overdue notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices is empty
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 13 October, as bounced
    • Then: Undelivered Notices lists an overdue-notice entry: Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, the cordless drill, due 12 October, failed 13 October, bounced.
  • Due date shown after an extension (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Loan Extended moved L1's due date to 19 October, and the loan is now overdue
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 20 October, as refused
    • Then: the entry shows the due date 19 October, failed 20 October, refused.
  • Pickup notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3a)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1 on 13 October, as refused
    • Then: Undelivered Notices also lists a pickup-notice entry: Ben Ito, ben@example.org, the hedge trimmer, collect by 16 October, failed 13 October, refused. Ana's entry is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-UDN-8)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry once
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Failed for L1 is applied again
    • Then: the entry is still listed once.
  • Tool returned (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: Ana's entry stays. It drops off once L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Someone else checks out the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1, and his collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: Cara checks the hedge trimmer out, so Hold Collected is recorded for her hold, not H1
    • Then: Ben's entry stays until Hold Expired is recorded for H1, and then drops off.
  • Holder cancels the hold (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while set aside (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Neighbor corrects their email (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry, showing ana@example.org, the address that bounced
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: Ana's entry shows ana.ruiz@example.net. The entry stays until L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Listing order (INV-UDN-9)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry (failed 13 October), Ana's overdue-notice entry (failed 14 October) and Ana's pickup-notice entry (failed 12 October)
    • When: the shed manager lists undelivered notices
    • Then: the entries come back as: Ana's pickup-notice entry, Ana's overdue-notice entry, then Ben's.
  • Listing undelivered notices
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry and Ben's pickup-notice entry
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists undelivered notices
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-UDN-8). An event applied a second time leaves the entries as they were after the first.
  • Ended loans and set-asides: a failure report for a loan or set-aside that has already ended is ignored by Record Overdue Notice Failure and Record Pickup Notice Failure, so no entry is ever created for one. An entry, once it drops off, never comes back.
  • No actions: the screen issues no commands. Its only use is to prompt the shed manager to follow up in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Undelivered Notices screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors never see it. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows neighbors' names, current emails and the tools they have or are waiting for, to the shed manager only. An entry is kept only while its loan or set-aside is live. Names and emails themselves are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, toolName, dueDate, reason, failedAt.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId, toolId, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, toolName, collectByDate, reason, failedAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId (the holder collecting ends the set-aside).
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs; the two failure events carrying the notice's details is agreed with slices/record-overdue-notice-failure.md and record-pickup-notice-failure.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen issues no commands.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Neighbors To Flag

Step 1 of 9 in Keep late returners in check · the story starts here · before Flag Neighbor · State View

Intent

The late-return flagger's to-do list: every neighbor whose late returns have reached the threshold (3 within 90 days) and who hasn't yet been flagged for them, with the loans those late returns belong to, each with the tool's name, the due date it missed and the date it came back. The flagger works through it, so the shed manager sees each of these neighbors flagged on Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Late Return Flagger, a system processor in the Flag Neighbor slice (slices/flag-neighbor.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the flagger does with it: for each neighbor returned, it issues Flag Neighbor naming the loans returned, which the flag uses up.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors To Flag built from events: "Tool Returned", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Late Return Flagger (Flag Neighbor). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events (seconds, not minutes). Which late returns are still within the 90 days is worked out when the list is read, from returnedOn and today's date in the shed's local time zone.

The view keeps one row for every late return that can still count toward a flag; the query groups them by neighbor. LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdTool Returned.neighborId: the borrower.
loanIdLoanIdTool Returned.loanId.
toolNameTextTool Returned.toolName. Carried onto the flag.
dueDateDateTool Returned.dueDate: the due date in force at the return. Carried onto the flag.
returnedOnDateTool Returned.returnedOn.
inWindowBoolDerived: yes while returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before it, in the shed's local time zone (INV-NTF-2). Worked out when the list is read.

To decide whether a return creates a row, the view also keeps, beyond its rows, every neighbor's current status: active, suspended (from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated) or closed (from Neighbor Account Closed). This is bookkeeping, not rows, and is never returned.

When a row is created. Tool Returned with late = yes creates a row for the loan's borrower, unless the borrower is suspended or their account is closed (INV-NTF-6, INV-NTF-7). An on-time return creates nothing. Lateness is read from Tool Returned.late, recorded once by Return Tool; this view never works it out.

When rows are removed.

  • Neighbor Flagged removes the rows for the loans it names as used up (INV-NTF-3).
  • Neighbor Suspended and Neighbor Reinstated remove all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-5, INV-NTF-7).
  • Neighbor Account Closed removes all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-6).

Nothing puts a row back.

Queries

  • List neighbors to flag. Takes nothing. Returns each neighbor who has at least 3 rows with inWindow yes, with their neighborId and those rows as late returns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn; all of them, if more than 3). There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the flagger.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NTF-1: Only late returns count toward the threshold.
    • Whether a return was late is recorded on Tool Returned (late), worked out by Return Tool against the loan's due date in force, after any extensions. A return on the due date is on time.
    • A loan that is still out doesn't count, even if it is overdue, until it is returned late.
    • A tool recorded lost never counts as a late return, even if the loan was overdue: it is never returned, so it never produces a Tool Returned.
  • INV-NTF-2: A neighbor is on the list when they have 3 or more late returns within the last 90 days that haven't counted toward a flag.
    • The 90 days are a rolling window, counted back from today by the date of each return. A late return older than that no longer counts. A late return counts on the day it was returned and the next 89 days, 90 calendar days in all, in the shed's local time. A return on 1 June counts through 29 August.
  • INV-NTF-3: Once Neighbor Flagged is recorded for a neighbor, the late returns it names are used up and never count again.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries every late return that counted when the flag was recorded. This list uses them up by loan; Neighbors shows them.
    • The neighbor leaves the list, and is flagged again only after 3 new late returns within 90 days.
    • A flag the shed manager doesn't act on stays open on Neighbors. It doesn't put the neighbor back on this list.
  • INV-NTF-5: Reinstatement starts a neighbor's late-return count again from zero.
    • Late returns from before Neighbor Reinstated never count toward a later flag.
  • INV-NTF-6: A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Account Closed is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it. An account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so no late return follows a closure.
  • INV-NTF-7: A suspended neighbor is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Suspended is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it, and late returns while they are suspended aren't counted. Reinstatement then starts their count again from zero.
  • INV-NTF-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The list has no screen; only the Late Return Flagger reads it. The shed manager sees flagged neighbors on Neighbors.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana is an active neighbor with no late returns counting, and today is 5 October.

  • On-time return doesn't count (INV-NTF-1)
    • Given: Ana's drill loan L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 on 12 October, with late = no
    • Then: no row is created, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Late return below the threshold (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has one late return counting, on 1 September
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L2 on 20 September, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has two late returns counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Third late return within 90 days (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 September (L1) and 20 September (L2)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L3 on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3.
  • Old late return has dropped out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns on 1 June and 20 September, neither used up
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: only two of Ana's late returns are within 90 days, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Four late returns in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1, 10 and 20 September, and the flagger hasn't acted yet
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with all four loans.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: those rows are removed, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Flagged again only on new late returns (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October, using up L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L4 on 12 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, L4, and she is not on the list.
  • Reinstatement resets the count (INV-NTF-5)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has since been reinstated, and had two late returns counting before her suspension
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 10 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Account closed while on the list (INV-NTF-6)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Suspended while on the list (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Late return while suspended (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan, with late = yes
    • Then: no row is created.
  • Last day in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 8 July, 20 September and 1 October; today is 5 October, which is 89 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 5 October
    • Then: all three are in the window, and the list returns Ana.
  • First day out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: as above, but today is 6 October, 90 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 6 October
    • Then: the 8 July return no longer counts, and the list doesn't return Ana.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NTF-8)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 and 20 September
    • When: the same Tool Returned for her 20 September return is applied again
    • Then: Ana still has two late returns counting.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NTF-8).
  • The flagger reads a neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands: the list may return the same neighbor on two reads in a row. Flagging once for the same late returns is Flag Neighbor's rule, enforced when it records Neighbor Flagged; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Late Return Flagger. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds neighbor and loan IDs and return dates only. No names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, neighborId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, lateReturns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn): the late returns it uses up.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match return-tool.md. Loan Extended is no longer read here: lateness comes from Tool Returned.late.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Late Return Flagger reads it and issues Flag Neighbor.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)

Slice: Flag Neighbor

Step 2 of 9 in Keep late returners in check · after Neighbors To Flag · before Neighbors — neighbor flagged · Automation

Intent

When a neighbor's late returns reach the late-return threshold, record that they crossed it, carrying the late returns behind the flag, so the shed manager sees them on Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them. The system flags; a person decides.

Trigger & Actor

Internally triggered. The Late Return Flagger, a system processor in this slice, acts whenever a neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, and issues Flag Neighbor for them with the loans that list gives. It is driven by events, not a schedule: a neighbor joins that list when a late return is recorded. No person flags a neighbor, and there is no screen. The neighbor isn't told; a flag is a prompt for the shed manager, not a penalty.

Command / Input

Command: Flag Neighbor

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's flaggedAt is that same moment.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor to flag. Must be a registered account (INV-FLG-10), not closed and not suspended (INV-FLG-5).
lateReturnsLateReturnFact[]yesThe late returns behind the flag, as Neighbors To Flag gave them: each a loanId, toolName, dueDate and returnedOn. Must be exactly the neighbor's counting late returns today, matched by loan (INV-FLG-4), and at least 3 of them (INV-FLG-2). Order doesn't matter.

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Late Return Flagger, also in this slice, reading Neighbors To Flag.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Flagged → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (the account's open flags: count, latest flag date and the late returns behind each) and Neighbors To Flag (the named late returns are used up).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command.
lateReturnsLateReturnFact[]yesFrom the command: the late returns this flag uses up, each with its loanId, toolName, dueDate and returnedOn. At least 3. Carried so Neighbors shows them without looking anything up.
flaggedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the flag date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. It carries the loans, not copies of names or dates; readers find each loan's tool and return date from its own events. A later flag records a new Neighbor Flagged.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Its processor reads Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md). Neighbor Flagged feeds Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) and takes the named late returns off Neighbors To Flag. Both are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A counting late return, for a neighbor today, is a loan of theirs whose Tool Returned has late yes, and which:

  • counts on its return day and the next 89 days: returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before, in the shed's local time;
  • isn't named by an earlier Neighbor Flagged for them;
  • was returned after their latest Neighbor Reinstated, if any;
  • was not returned while they were suspended.

A tool recorded lost has no Tool Returned, so it never counts. Once flagged, the neighbor shows as flagged on Neighbors until the shed manager acts; there is no dismiss action (Neighbors owns how it shows). Neighbors are flagged by the system only, through the processor above.

  • INV-FLG-2: A neighbor is flagged when they have at least 3 counting late returns.
    • "At least 3" is tested on the neighbor's own counting set, worked out from their events when the command is handled, not on the loans the command names. Loans that don't count are never made up for by naming them.
  • INV-FLG-3: Flagging never suspends anyone.
    • Flag Neighbor records only Neighbor Flagged. The shed manager decides whether to suspend a flagged neighbor (Suspend Neighbor).
  • INV-FLG-4: A flag uses up the late returns that caused it.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries every counting late return the neighbor has when it is recorded, even if there are more than 3. Those loans never count again.
    • The neighbor is flagged again only after 3 new counting late returns.
  • INV-FLG-5: A neighbor is flagged only while they are still due a flag.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged, and nor is a suspended neighbor. A neighbor whose count was reset by reinstatement after they joined Neighbors To Flag is not flagged for those late returns.
  • INV-FLG-7: A neighbor flagged again while an earlier flag is still open on Neighbors gets a second Neighbor Flagged.
    • An earlier flag never stops a new one. Neighbors keeps one row for the neighbor, with the count and the latest date.
  • INV-FLG-9: Flagging a neighbor again for exactly the loans an earlier Neighbor Flagged already names succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-FLG-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-3, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active, with late returns of loans L1 on 1 September, L2 on 20 September and L3 on 5 October, none named by an earlier flag. It is 5 October.
    • When: the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Four counting late returns (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded naming all four.
  • A loan left out (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with only L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." No event is recorded.
  • Below the threshold (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1 and L2 only
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1 and L2
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." No event is recorded.
  • A late return drops out of the window (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 1 June, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." The 1 June return is more than 90 days back. No event is recorded.
  • Window boundary (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 8 July, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded: 8 July is the 89th day before 5 October, so it still counts.
  • Flagged again on new late returns (INV-FLG-4, INV-FLG-7)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October for L1, L2 and L3, and the shed manager hasn't acted. Since then she returned L5, L6 and L7 late, on 20 October, 1 November and 15 November.
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L5, L6 and L7 on 15 November
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded again, naming L5, L6 and L7.
  • Used-up returns don't count again (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and returned L5 late since
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L5
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Only L5 counts. No event is recorded.
  • An old loan named alongside new ones (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and has since returned L5, L6 and L7 late
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L5, L6 and L7
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." L1 was used up by the earlier flag. No event is recorded.
  • The same flag arrives twice (INV-FLG-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Flagged was recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3 is issued again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, with 3 late returns from before her suspension that were never flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "This neighbor is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Count reset by reinstatement (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana returned L1, L2 and L3 late, then was suspended and reinstated
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Returns from before her reinstatement don't count. No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana's account was closed after she reached 3 counting late returns
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-FLG-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Late Return Flagger logs it with the neighbor ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. neighbor-not-found (INV-FLG-10).
  2. If a Neighbor Flagged for this neighbor already names exactly these loans, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9).
  3. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-FLG-5).
  4. below-threshold (INV-FLG-2).
  5. late-returns-changed, if the loans given aren't exactly the neighbor's counting late returns (INV-FLG-4).
ReasonSentenceRule
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-FLG-10
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-FLG-5
neighbor-suspendedThis neighbor is suspended.INV-FLG-5
below-thresholdThis neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count.INV-FLG-2
late-returns-changedThe late returns behind this flag have changed.INV-FLG-4

neighbor-not-found, account-closed and neighbor-suspended mean the same conditions as in the neighbor commands; the sentences here fit a system log. A missing or malformed ID, or an empty loan list, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Flag Neighbor with the same loans succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9). The flagger may act on the same neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands; the second command is then a repeat.

late-returns-changed means the list moved on between the flagger's read and the command, for example a fourth late return landed. The flagger acts again on the list's updated entry, which gives the current set.

Requests at the same moment: Flag Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A suspension, reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed when a neighbor is flagged.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor. No person or screen does. It is an internal automation command, not on the REST API, so it has no sign-in guard.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Flagged links a neighbor to loans they returned late. It holds no name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the list's freshness. The flagger acts as soon as the neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, shortly after the late return that crosses the threshold is recorded.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, neighborId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (this slice): neighborId, lateReturns.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md and slices/return-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md): each neighbor due a flag, with all their counting late returns.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and Neighbors To Flag. Suspend Neighbor is offered on Neighbors.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)

Slice: Neighbors

Step 2 of 6 in Join the shed · after Register Neighbor · before My Account · State View

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor account that has signed up, with each account's current status (active, suspended or closed), on the Neighbors screen. It is the shed manager's one screen for neighbors: it shows who the system has flagged for repeated late returns and the late returns behind each flag, who is suspended and since when, and account closures, and it is the screen the shed manager suspends and reinstates neighbors from. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Version 2 folds the former Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors views into this one: both were filters of the same accounts, and each offered one action this screen now offers.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per account ever registered, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Suspend (Suspend Neighbor slice) — offered on every active account, flagged or not (INV-NBRS-6).
    • Reinstate (Reinstate Neighbor slice) — offered on every suspended account (INV-NBRS-13).
  • Flagging is done by the system (Flag Neighbor). A neighbor is not told they were flagged, and a suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag, INV-NTF-7). No email goes to the neighbor on suspension or reinstatement, and no reason or note is recorded with a suspension.
  • Showing only the flagged accounts, or only the suspended ones, is the screen's own filter over this one list; there is no separate read model for either.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Suspend and Reinstate check their own rules when they run, so a stale entry can't suspend someone who is no longer active or reinstate someone who is no longer suspended.

One row per account. NeighborId, LoanId and ToolId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdNeighbor Registered.neighborId.
nameTextNeighbor Registered.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
emailTextNeighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the account's current email.
registeredAtInstantNeighbor Registered.registeredAt. Shown as the sign-up date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone (INV-NBRS-5).
statusTextOne of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
suspendedAtInstantDerived: suspendedAt of the Neighbor Suspended behind a suspended status; empty otherwise (INV-NBRS-12). Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
flagCountIntDerived: the number of open flags on the account: Neighbor Flagged recorded since the account was last suspended, or ever if never suspended (INV-NBRS-10, INV-NBRS-11). 0 when the account is not flagged.
latestFlaggedAtInstantDerived: flaggedAt of the latest open flag; empty when flagCount is 0. Shown as a date in the shed's local time zone.
lateReturnsLateReturn[]Derived: one item for each loan named by the account's open flags, as below; empty when flagCount is 0.
canSuspendBoolDerived: yes while status is active (INV-NBRS-6).
canReinstateBoolDerived: yes while status is suspended (INV-NBRS-13).

Each LateReturn item:

FieldTypeSource / Notes
loanIdLoanIdNeighbor Flagged.lateReturns[].loanId.
toolNameTextNeighbor Flagged.lateReturns[].toolName.
dueDateDateNeighbor Flagged.lateReturns[].dueDate: the due date in force when it was returned.
returnedOnDateNeighbor Flagged.lateReturns[].returnedOn.
flaggedAtInstantflaggedAt of the Neighbor Flagged that named this loan.

The view keeps nothing beyond its rows: a flag carries its late returns (INV-NBRS-14).

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Flag rules. A flag is open from its Neighbor Flagged until the account is next suspended or closed; suspension and closure clear the account's open flags (INV-NBRS-11). A Neighbor Flagged recorded after a reinstatement starts the account's flags afresh.

Queries

  • List the neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every account, each with every field above, including its late returns. There is no paging: the query always returns every account, ordered by name, then by registeredAt (INV-NBRS-8). The screen filters to flagged (flagCount above 0) or suspended accounts itself.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NBRS-1: Every account appears on the Neighbors screen exactly once.
    • One entry per Neighbor Registered; nothing else creates an entry. A neighbor who signs up again after closing their account has a new account, so they appear twice: the closed entry and the new one.
  • INV-NBRS-2: Each account's status is active, suspended or closed, worked out by the status rules above.
    • Neighbor Registered → active. Neighbor Suspended → suspended. Neighbor Reinstated → active. Neighbor Account Closed → closed.
  • INV-NBRS-3: An account that is closed stays listed, shown as closed.
    • This screen is where the shed manager sees account closures. It is the record of every account; a closed account keeps its row, with no action offered and no open flags.
  • INV-NBRS-4: Closed is final.
    • A suspended neighbor who closes their account shows as closed, not suspended. No later event changes a closed account's status.
  • INV-NBRS-5: Each entry shows the account's name, its current email, its sign-up date, and its status.
    • The email is set by Neighbor Registered and replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed. The name never changes.
  • INV-NBRS-6: The screen offers Suspend on every active account, whether or not the neighbor has been flagged, and on no other.
    • Suspend Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-8: Accounts are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they signed up.
    • So a neighbor who signed up again after closing appears twice, the older account first.
  • INV-NBRS-7: Applying the same event twice leaves the Neighbors screen as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-NBRS-9: Only the shed manager can read the Neighbors screen.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.
  • INV-NBRS-10: A flagged account shows how many open flags it has, the date of the latest, and the late returns behind every open flag, each with the tool's name, its due date, the date it was returned, and the date of the flag that named it.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries the late returns it uses up: each loan with the tool's name, the due date in force at the return, and the return date. The view copies them.
    • Being flagged never suspends anyone by itself, and there is no dismiss action: a flag the shed manager decides not to act on stays open.
  • INV-NBRS-11: Suspending or closing the account clears its open flags; a flag recorded after a reinstatement starts the count afresh.
    • The flags were what the shed manager acted on, or can no longer act on. A suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag), so no flag lands while suspended.
  • INV-NBRS-12: A suspended account shows when it was suspended; the date is cleared on reinstatement.
    • A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time, and it is never permanent. A neighbor suspended again after a reinstatement shows the new date.
  • INV-NBRS-13: The screen offers Reinstate on every suspended account, and on no other.
    • Reinstate Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-14: The view keeps no bookkeeping beyond its rows: every event that changes a row carries what the row shows.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and Ben Ito with ben@example.org. Ana returned the ladder (L1, due 31 August) on 1 September, the drill (L2, due 15 September) on 20 September and the hedge trimmer (L3, due 1 October) on 5 October, all late.

  • Neighbor registered (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-6)
    • Given: no neighbors have signed up
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, signed up on today's date, as active, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-NBRS-1)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a different account, also named Ana Ruiz, with ana.r@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists both, as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NBRS-7)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana once, as active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for Ana is applied again
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana once.
  • Email changed (INV-NBRS-5)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org, as active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana.ruiz@example.net, still active.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 5 October, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, latest on 5 October, with three late returns: the ladder (due 31 August, returned 1 September), the drill (due 15 September, returned 20 September) and the hedge trimmer (due 1 October, returned 5 October). Suspend is offered, as before.
  • Due date after an extension (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: L2 was extended from 15 September to 18 September before it was returned on 20 September
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the drill's late return shows due 18 September, returned 20 September.
  • Flagged again (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once on 5 October, and she has since returned three more tools late (L4, L5, L6)
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 15 November, naming L4, L5 and L6
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged twice, latest on 15 November, with all six late returns: L1, L2 and L3 flagged 5 October, and L4, L5 and L6 flagged 15 November.
  • Flag left alone (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has shown Ana flagged since 5 October, and the shed manager has not suspended her
    • When: a month passes with no Neighbor Suspended recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana is still shown flagged once, with the same late returns.
  • Flagged neighbor changes their email (INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net. Her flags are unchanged.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, and Ben as active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana on 7 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October, with no open flags, Suspend not offered and Reinstate offered. Ben is unchanged.
  • Suspended without a flag (INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ben on 9 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as suspended since 9 October, with Reinstate offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active again, with no suspended date, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Flagged again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: Ana was flagged, then suspended, which cleared her flags, and later reinstated
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 20 January, naming L7, L8 and L9
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once, latest on 20 January, with only L7, L8 and L9.
  • Suspended again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: Ana was suspended on 7 October and reinstated on 1 November
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana again on 3 February
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 3 February.
  • Account closed (INV-NBRS-3, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana, now shown as closed, with no open flags and neither Suspend nor Reinstate offered.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-NBRS-4, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as closed, with Reinstate not offered.
  • Closed stays closed (INV-NBRS-4)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana's account as closed
    • When: an earlier Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Flagged for that account is applied again
    • Then: the account is still shown as closed, with no open flags.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-3)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz's account, ana@example.org, as closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account for Ana Ruiz, with ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists two entries for Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org: the old account, still closed, and the new one, active, with Suspend offered.
  • Listing order (INV-NBRS-8)
    • Given: Ben Ito signed up on 2 October; Ana Ruiz signed up on 1 October, closed her account, and signed up again on 5 October
    • When: the shed manager lists the neighbors
    • Then: the accounts come back as: Ana Ruiz (signed up 1 October, closed), Ana Ruiz (signed up 5 October, active), then Ben Ito.
  • Listing the neighbors
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana (active, flagged once), Ben (suspended) and Cara (closed)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the neighbors
    • Then: all three are returned with all their fields, Ana's with her late returns, with no paging. Only Ana's entry offers Suspend; only Ben's offers Reinstate.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NBRS-7). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for an account the view hasn't seen: events are applied in the order they were recorded, and every account starts with Neighbor Registered, so this can't happen.
  • Events on a closed account: a Neighbor Flagged, Neighbor Suspended or Neighbor Reinstated applied to a closed account changes nothing (INV-NBRS-4).
  • Stale actions: Suspend or Reinstate offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor check their own rules and refuse with their own reasons; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors see only their own account, on My Account. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows every account's name, current email, sign-up date, status, suspension date and late-return history to the shed manager, including closed accounts, which stay listed. A replaced email is not kept in the view. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and are never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email, registeredAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, lateReturns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn), flaggedAt.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId, suspendedAt.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/register-neighbor.md, flag-neighbor.md, suspend-neighbor.md and the loan slices' docs.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor.
  • Lineage: v2 merges Flagged Neighbors v1 and Suspended Neighbors v1 into this view (model reshape, 2026-11-01). Their docs stay in slices/ marked superseded by neighbors@v2.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Suspend Neighbor

Step 4 of 9 in Keep late returners in check · after Neighbors — neighbor flagged · before Neighbors — neighbor suspended · State Change

Intent

Let the shed manager suspend any active neighbor, so someone who keeps returning tools late stops borrowing until the shed manager reinstates them. Usually the neighbor has been flagged for late returns. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager issues Suspend Neighbor from the Neighbors screen, for any active neighbor, flagged or not. The usual case is a neighbor the system has flagged for late returns, whose flags and late returns the screen shows; it also covers a neighbor who closed their account while suspended and signed up again with a different email.

The system never suspends anyone: reaching the late-return threshold only flags a neighbor. (Version 1 drew this trigger from a separate Flagged Neighbors screen; v2 folds that screen into Neighbors.)

Command / Input

Command: Suspend Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
neighborIdNeighborIdyesThe neighbor to suspend. Must be a registered account (INV-SUS-10) that isn't closed (INV-SUS-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The flag and its late returns are usually the reason, and a suspension from the Neighbors screen needs none. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Neighbors @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Suspended → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (status suspended, the suspended date, the open flags cleared, Reinstate offered), My Account (status suspended), and Neighbors To Flag (a suspended neighbor is never flagged). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to refuse a suspended neighbor.

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdyesFrom the command.
suspendedAtInstantyesThe UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Reinstated lifts the suspension; a later suspension records a new Neighbor Suspended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Suspended feeds Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Suspension's effects are rules of the slices that refuse a suspended neighbor, each with its own reason the neighbor can see: a suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, including one set aside for them (INV-CHK-7, Check Out Tool), extend a loan (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan), place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9, Place Hold) or change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email). They keep what they already have: their loans stay out and they can return them (INV-RET-7, Return Tool), and their holds keep their places and can be cancelled. A set-aside they can't collect expires at the end of its collect-by date, as any other (Expire Hold). While suspended they are never flagged (Flag Neighbor, INV-FLG-5). A suspension lasts until the shed manager reinstates the neighbor (Reinstate Neighbor); it never lifts by itself and is never permanent. The neighbor isn't emailed: they see the suspension on My Account and as the reason whenever something is refused. Neighbors and My Account own how a suspension is shown.

  • INV-SUS-1: Only the shed manager suspends a neighbor.
    • Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • INV-SUS-2: Only an active neighbor can be suspended.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be suspended, because closed is final.
    • Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended changes nothing (INV-SUS-9).
  • INV-SUS-9: Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second suspension.
  • INV-SUS-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-SUS-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: suspending a flagged neighbor (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active and shown flagged on Neighbors after three late returns within 90 days. She has the ladder on loan and a hold waiting on the cordless drill.
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 from Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her loan and her hold are untouched.
  • Suspending a neighbor who isn't flagged (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is active and not flagged
    • When: the shed manager suspends N2 from the Neighbors screen
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2.
  • Suspending again after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and later reinstated, so she is active
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1
    • Then: a new Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1.
  • Already suspended (INV-SUS-9)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A late copy after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: the shed manager suspended N1, and then reinstated her
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Suspend Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed account (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N3's account is closed
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N4 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N4
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." Its status is closed, not suspended, so this isn't treated as a repeat. No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-SUS-1)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to suspend N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-SUS-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to suspend N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-SUS-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for suspending a neighbor arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the screen they acted from. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-SUS-11): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-SUS-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-SUS-10).
  4. If the neighbor's status is already suspended, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-SUS-9). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed, not the repeat.
  5. account-closed (INV-SUS-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-SUS-11
not-shed-managerOnly the shed manager can suspend neighbors.INV-SUS-1
neighbor-not-foundThere is no such neighbor.INV-SUS-10
account-closedThis account is closed.INV-SUS-2

not-shed-manager, neighbor-not-found and account-closed mean the same conditions as in Add Tool, Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screens, which offer Suspend only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: suspension is a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is suspended) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a reinstatement suspends again.

Requests at the same moment: Suspend Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may suspend a neighbor (INV-SUS-1). Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Suspended links a neighbor to a suspension. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered matches slices/register-neighbor.md. Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor refuse a suspended neighbor; Reinstate Neighbor lifts the suspension.

Open Questions

None.
