State Viewv1ImplementedIn sync

Slice: My Account

Step 3 of 6 in Join the shed · after Neighbors · before Change Email · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor their own account on the My Account screen: their name, their current email, and whether the account is active, suspended or closed. It is where a neighbor learns they are suspended, and the screen they change their email and close their account from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Account screen. A neighbor whose account is closed can still open it, read-only.
  • Whose account it shows: the account of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Change Email (Change Email slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9).
    • Close Account (Close Account slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-11).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Account built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Account screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because Change Email and Close Account each check their own rules when they run.

One row per account. A NeighborId is a UUID. An Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
neighborIdNeighborIdNeighbor Registered.neighborId.
nameTextNeighbor Registered.name. Never changes.
emailTextNeighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the current one.
statusTextOne of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
canChangeEmailBoolDerived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-9).
canCloseAccountBoolDerived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-11).

My Account doesn't show the neighbor's sign-up date; that is the shed manager's to see, on Neighbors.

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account. Closed is final.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Queries

  • Get my account. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns that one account with every field above, or not found if no account has that neighbor ID. It never returns another account (INV-MYAC-1).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYAC-1: A neighbor's My Account shows only their own account.
    • The query returns the one account whose neighbor ID it is given, and nothing about any other account.
  • INV-MYAC-2: My Account shows the neighbor's name and their current email.
    • Neighbor Registered sets the email. Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The name never changes after sign-up.
  • INV-MYAC-3: A newly registered neighbor's account shows as active.
    • One account per Neighbor Registered.
  • INV-MYAC-4: A suspended neighbor's account shows as suspended until they are reinstated, and then shows as active again.
    • This is how a neighbor learns they are suspended; they aren't emailed about it.
  • INV-MYAC-5: Once a neighbor closes their account, it shows as closed, permanently.
    • Closed is final. A suspended neighbor who closes their account sees it as closed, not suspended.
  • INV-MYAC-6: After closing their account, the neighbor can still view My Account, read-only.
    • Close Account and Change Email are no longer offered on a closed account.
  • INV-MYAC-7: Only Neighbor Registered, Neighbor Email Changed, Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated and Neighbor Account Closed change My Account.
    • Loans, holds and flags never change it.
  • INV-MYAC-8: A person who signs up again after closing an account has a new account, and My Account shows them only that new account.
    • Each account has its own neighbor ID, and the query returns the one account it is asked for. The old, closed account is no longer shown to them. It stays on the shed manager's Neighbors screen.
  • INV-MYAC-9: My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered to a suspended neighbor too. Change Email refuses them with its own reason (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), and they can change it once reinstated. A refusal with a reason they see means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-10: Applying the same event twice leaves My Account as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYAC-11: My Account offers Close Account on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered whether or not the neighbor has tools on loan. Close Account refuses a neighbor with tools on loan with its own reason (INV-CLS-7, Close Account): a refusal with a reason the neighbor sees means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-13: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYAC-14: My Account is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Neighbor registered (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-3, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N1
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and the email ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active, with Change Email and Close Account offered.
  • Email changed (INV-MYAC-2)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-MYAC-4, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows suspended. Change Email and Close Account are still offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows active.
  • Email changed after reinstatement (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and then reinstated, and My Account for N1 shows ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Account closed (INV-MYAC-5, INV-MYAC-6)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, with neither Change Email nor Close Account offered. It can still be read.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-MYAC-5)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, not suspended.
  • Signed up again after closing (INV-MYAC-8)
    • Given: account N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, is closed, and was not suspended when it was closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account N4, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N4 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active. My Account for N1 still shows closed; asking for N4 never returns N1.
  • Only their own account (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: accounts N1 (Ana) and N2 (Ben) are both registered
    • When: My Account is asked for N1
    • Then: it returns Ana's account only. Nothing about Ben's account is returned.
  • Another neighbor's change (INV-MYAC-1, INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Loans and holds don't change it (INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for N1, and later Hold Placed for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYAC-10)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for N1 is applied again
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged, and there is still one account N1.
  • Asking for an account that doesn't exist (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: My Account is asked for N9
    • Then: not found.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYAC-13)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYAC-14)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for N1, Ana's account
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own account." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYAC-13
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own account.INV-MYAC-14
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYAC-10). An event applied a second time leaves the account as it was after the first.
  • Events for a closed account: closed is final, so no Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for a closed account (Close Account: nothing reopens, suspends or reinstates a closed account; Change Email, INV-CEM-3). If one reaches this view, it can only be a replay, and it changes nothing.
  • Unknown neighbor ID: the query returns not found. The screen shows that no account was found rather than an error.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Change Email just after the neighbor was suspended). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may read only their own account (INV-MYAC-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  • PII & compliance: holds and shows the neighbor's name and email, to that neighbor only. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased, including a closed account's.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Change Email, Suspend Neighbor, Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account aren't yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Change Email and Close Account.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":65,"name":"Retire Tool","x0":11147.76,"x1":11291.76,"docHtml":"
State Changev2DraftDelta pending

Slice: Retire Tool

Step 1 of 15 in Take a tool or a neighbor out of the shed · the story starts here · before My Holds — tool retired · State Change

Intent

Take a tool out of the shed for good: a damaged tool, one the shed no longer keeps, or one added with a mistake. The shed manager retires it from Tool Inventory, and neighbors can no longer borrow or hold it. Retiring is final: nothing un-retires a tool. A tool retired to correct a mistake in its details is added again as a new tool.

What follows a retirement is decided by the views and slices that read Tool Retired:

  • The tool drops off the Tool Catalog at once (INV-TCAT-8). It drops off Tool Inventory at once if it is in the shed. A tool retired while on loan stays on Tool Inventory, shown as retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost (INV-TINV-2), so the shed manager can still record it lost if it never comes back.
  • Every hold on the tool ends, waiting or set aside: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for each in the same decision. No hold is passed on, and the holders are not told; their holds drop off My Holds (INV-MYHD-7).
  • A loan on the tool carries on, can't be extended (INV-EXT-8), and ends when the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • Check Out Tool and Place Hold refuse a retired tool.

A tool lost or broken by a borrower, and never returned, is not retired here. The shed manager records it lost against the loan (Record Tool Lost), which ends the loan and retires the tool in one step. A lost tool that later turns up is added again as a new tool.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, which offers Retire on every listed tool not already retired (INV-TINV-7). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role.

Command / Input

Command: Retire Tool

A ToolId is a UUID.

FieldTypeRequiredRules / Validation
toolIdToolIdyesThe tool to retire. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-RTR-10). It may be in the shed, on loan, reserved or set aside (INV-RTR-6).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Retired → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is retired) and My Loans (a loan on it is marked).

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
toolIdToolIdyesFrom the command.
retiredAtInstantyesSet by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

Nothing is recorded about the tool's condition or the reason it was retired: the event carries no reason, note or condition. A damaged tool is the shed manager's call to retire.

Event: Hold Cancelled → context Holds Read by: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire, Pickup Notices To Send and Undelivered Notices, as any cancellation (the hold ends).

The same event Cancel Hold records, recorded here once per hold on the tool, waiting or set aside, in the same decision as Tool Retired. The decider reads the holds it ends. With no such hold, none is recorded; the readers can't tell these from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.

FieldTypeImmutable Fact?Source / Notes
holdIdHoldIdyesSet by the system: the hold being ended, from its Hold Placed.
cancelledAtInstantyesSet by the system: the same moment as Tool Retired.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Retired changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog and marks a loan on it in My Loans; the Hold Cancelled recorded with it end its holds in My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-RTR-1: Only the shed manager can retire a tool.
    • Neighbors do not retire tools. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused with not-shed-manager.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in, before anything else is checked.
  • INV-RTR-2: Retiring a tool that is already retired records nothing new.
    • The request succeeds, so a double submit or a retry never fails and never records a second Tool Retired. This includes a tool retired by being recorded lost.
  • INV-RTR-6: A tool can be retired whatever its state: in the shed, on loan, reserved or set aside.
    • Retiring is never refused because of a loan or a hold.
  • INV-RTR-10: The tool must exist.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the ladder is in the shed, available, with no holds on it
    • When: the shed manager retires the ladder from Tool Inventory
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder, and nothing else.
  • Tool set aside, another hold waiting (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the cordless drill is set aside for Ben, and Cara's hold on it is waiting
    • When: the shed manager retires the drill
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold and for Cara's.
  • Tool on loan, with a hold waiting (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: Ana has the hedge trimmer on loan, due 20 October, and Ben's hold on it is waiting
    • When: the shed manager retires the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold. Ana's loan is unchanged.
  • Tool reserved (INV-RTR-6)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned with Ben's hold waiting, and Hold Fulfilled hasn't been recorded yet
    • When: the shed manager retires the drill
    • Then: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill, and Hold Cancelled for Ben's hold.
  • Retiring twice (INV-RTR-2)
    • Given: Tool Retired has been recorded for the ladder
    • When: the shed manager retires the ladder again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Retiring a tool recorded lost (INV-RTR-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for Ana's loan of the hedge trimmer, which retired it
    • When: the shed manager retires the hedge trimmer
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-RTR-1)
    • Given: the ladder is in the shed
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to retire it
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can retire tools." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-RTR-10)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: the shed manager retires T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • No sign-in (INV-RTR-1)
    • Given: a caller with no sign-in
    • When: they ask to retire the ladder
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in, then not-shed-manager (INV-RTR-1).
  2. tool-not-found (INV-RTR-10).
  3. If the tool is already retired, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-RTR-2).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-RTR-1
not-shed-managerOnly the shed manager can retire tools.INV-RTR-1
tool-not-foundThere is no such tool.INV-RTR-10

not-shed-manager and tool-not-found mean the same conditions as in Add Tool and Check Out Tool. tool-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: retiring a tool that is already retired succeeds and records nothing (INV-RTR-2).

Requests at the same moment: Retire Tool is decided against the tool's events as already recorded, one at a time per tool. If a checkout, a hold or a fulfilment for the tool is decided just before the retirement, it stands, and the retirement then ends the loan's chance of extension and the tool's holds. If it is decided just after, it is refused by its own slice because the tool is retired.

There are no external calls in this slice, and no email is sent.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may retire a tool (INV-RTR-1). Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Retired holds only the tool and a time.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Retired (this slice): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId (a lost tool is retired by that).
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs and the loan-ending convention.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans (Tool Retired); My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (the Hold Cancelled recorded here). Check Out Tool, Place Hold, Extend Loan and Fulfill Hold read whether a tool is retired.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":66,"name":"My Holds — tool retired","x0":11316.76,"x1":11460.76,"docHtml":"
State Viewv2DraftDelta pending

Slice: My Holds

Step 2 of 29 in Hold a tool for pickup · after Place Hold · before Tool Catalog — hold placed · State View

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
holdIdHoldIdHold Placed.holdId.
neighborIdNeighborIdHold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolIdToolIdHold Placed.toolId.
toolNameTextHold Placed.toolName (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAtInstantHold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
statusTextOne of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
positionIntDerived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDateDateDerived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNoticeTextOne of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancelBoolDerived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, or when the holder checks the tool out. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Hold Collected for the hold (the holder checked the tool out).

Retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each end holds by recording Hold Cancelled for them (Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost, Close Account). This view hears only the Holds events.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when the hold was placed, in the order Hold Placed was recorded (INV-MYHD-18).

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position. No neighbor-facing screen ever shows who has a tool or who holds one; only the shed manager sees borrowers, on Tool Inventory.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost record Hold Cancelled for each hold; this view hears those. The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of the neighbor's holds; this view hears those.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes with Hold Placed, which carries it.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed and Hold Expired change My Holds.
    • A checkout records Hold Collected only when the borrower had a hold on the tool; a checkout by anyone else is not heard here at all.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.
  • INV-MYHD-18: Holds are listed by tool name, ignoring case, then by when they were placed.
  • INV-MYHD-19: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYHD-20: My Holds is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ana has T1, the "Cordless drill", on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1, carrying the name "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1, before any Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Retired for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Record Tool Lost records Hold Cancelled for H1 and for H2, with Tool Lost for L1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • List order (INV-MYHD-18)
    • Given: Ben placed H5 on the ladder, then H1 on the cordless drill
    • When: his holds are listed
    • Then: H1 (cordless drill) comes first, then H5 (ladder).
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYHD-19)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Holds is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYHD-20)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: the holds of N1, Ana, are asked for
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own holds." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-MYHD-19
requester-mismatchYou can only see your own holds.INV-MYHD-20
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYHD-20), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYHD-19).
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Collected (Collect Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end; this view can't tell those from a holder's own cancellation and needn't.
    • Hold Placed and Hold Collected match slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Tool Inventory

Step 2 of 3 in Stock the shed · after Add Tool · before Tool Catalog · State View

Intent

Shows the shed manager every tool in the shed on the Tool Inventory screen, and which of them are out on loan, to whom, and until when. It is the shed manager's working screen for tools: they add and retire tools from it, and record a tool lost when it is out and never coming back.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Tool Inventory screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool currently in the shed or out on loan, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Add Tool (Add Tool slice) — always offered.
    • Retire (Retire Tool slice) — offered on every listed tool that is not already retired (INV-TINV-7).
    • Mark lost (Record Tool Lost slice) — offered only on a tool that is out on loan (INV-TINV-6).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Inventory built from events: "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Inventory screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual — an entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because each command checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
toolIdToolIdTool Added.toolId.
nameTextTool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
descriptionTextOptional: absent when the tool was added without one. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDaysIntTool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays (1–30).
addedAtInstantTool Added.addedAt.
onLoanBoolDerived: yes from Tool Checked Out for this tool until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan; no otherwise.
loanIdLoanIdDerived: Tool Checked Out.loanId while the tool is on loan; none once Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan lands. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerIdNeighborIdDerived: Tool Checked Out.neighborId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerNameTextTool Checked Out.neighborName while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
dueDateDateDerived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
retiredBoolDerived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for this tool. A retired row exists only while the tool is still out on loan.
canRetireBoolDerived: yes while retired is no. Returned so the screen can offer Retire (INV-TINV-7).
overdueBoolDerived: yes while the tool is on loan and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate; no otherwise (INV-TINV-9). Worked out when the inventory is read.
canMarkLostBoolDerived: same as onLoan. Returned so the screen can offer Mark lost (INV-TINV-6).

Queries

  • List the tool inventory. Takes nothing. Returns every listed tool, each with all the fields above. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool. Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added (addedAt); tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded (INV-TINV-10).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TINV-1: Every added tool appears in the inventory exactly once.
    • One entry per Tool Added; nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each physical item is its own tool, so two identical drills are two entries.
  • INV-TINV-2: A retired tool drops off the inventory once it is back in the shed or recorded lost.
    • A tool retired while it is in the shed drops off at once.
    • A tool retired while it is out on loan stays listed, marked retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost. Then it drops off. This lets the shed manager record it lost if it never comes back.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it drops off too.
    • This differs from the Tool Catalog, where a tool retired while on loan drops off at once: neighbors can do nothing with it, while the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TINV-3: The inventory changes only when a tool is added, checked out, extended, returned, retired or recorded lost.
    • The borrower's name shown on a tool that is out comes with Tool Checked Out.
    • Holds and overdue notices leave it unchanged. Hold state is shown to neighbors on the Tool Catalog, not here.
    • A tool's details never change after it is added (see the note under Add Tool's event table). A mistake is corrected by retiring the tool and adding it again.
  • INV-TINV-4: Each entry shows the tool's name, its description when it has one, and its default checkout period.
  • INV-TINV-5: Each entry shows whether the tool is out on loan. A tool that is out also shows the borrower's name and the due date.
    • A tool is out from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost.
    • The due date moves with each extension.
    • When the tool comes back or is recorded lost, the borrower's name and due date are no longer shown on it.
  • INV-TINV-6: The inventory offers "mark lost" only on a tool that is out on loan.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires the tool and ends its holds. It never counts as a late return for the borrower (Record Tool Lost).
  • INV-TINV-7: The inventory offers "retire" on every listed tool that is not already retired.
    • A tool retired while out on loan stays listed but is not offered "retire" again.
  • INV-TINV-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the inventory as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TINV-9: A tool that is out shows whether its loan is overdue.
    • Overdue means today's date in the shed's local time zone is after the due date in force. It is worked out when the inventory is read; no event marks a loan overdue.
  • INV-TINV-10: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • Tools with the same name are in the order they were added; tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded.
  • INV-TINV-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-TINV-12: Only the shed manager can read the Tool Inventory: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TINV-1, INV-TINV-4, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill with its description and its 7-day default checkout period, in the shed, with "retire" offered and no "mark lost".
  • Tool added without a description (INV-TINV-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a ladder with no description and a default checkout period of 3 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the ladder with its 3-day default checkout period and no description.
  • Two of the same tool (INV-TINV-1)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists one cordless drill
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second cordless drill, with its own tool ID
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TINV-8)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill once
    • When: the same Tool Added for that drill is applied again
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the drill once.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill, in the shed
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for Ana Ruiz borrowing the drill, due 12 October, carrying her name
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as out on loan to Ana Ruiz, due 12 October, and offers "mark lost" on it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TINV-5)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for Ana's drill loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October.
  • Tool returned (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as in the shed, with no borrower, due date or "mark lost".
  • Tool retired (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists a cordless drill and a ladder, both in the shed
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: the cordless drill drops off the Tool Inventory, and the ladder is still listed.
  • Tool retired while out on loan (INV-TINV-2, INV-TINV-6, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder out on loan to Ben, due 20 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the ladder, marked retired and out on loan to Ben, due 20 October, with "mark lost" still offered and "retire" no longer offered.
  • Retired tool comes back (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Retired tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the hedge trimmer out on loan to Ana
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ana's hedge trimmer loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Out tool becomes overdue (INV-TINV-9)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: the inventory is read at 23:59 on 12 October, and again at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: the drill shows not overdue on the first read and overdue on the second. Nothing is recorded.
  • List order (INV-TINV-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for "Ladder", then "Cordless drill", then a second "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: the order is the first "Cordless drill", the second "Cordless drill", then "Ladder".
  • Holds and notices don't change it (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben on the drill, and later Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing the inventory
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill (in the shed) and the ladder (out on loan to Ben, due 20 October)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: both tools are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • Not signed in (INV-TINV-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-TINV-12)
    • Given: a neighbor is signed in, without the shed-manager role
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12).
ReasonSentenceRule
not-signed-inPlease sign in.INV-TINV-11
not-shed-managerOnly the shed manager can see the tool inventory.INV-TINV-12
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TINV-8). A Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Tool Returned, Tool Retired or Tool Lost applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: under the rules above, a Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost can reach this view for a tool that is no longer listed only as a replay of an event already applied. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, "mark lost" on a tool that has just been returned). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Inventory is the shed manager's screen; neighbors see tools on the Tool Catalog instead. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  • PII & compliance: shows a borrower's name while they have a tool out. It never shows their email. The name stops being shown on that tool once the loan ends.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, neighborName, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • All but Tool Added are specified in slices not yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Add Tool, Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Tool Catalog

Step 3 of 3 in Stock the shed · after Tool Inventory · the story ends here · State View

Intent

Shows neighbors every tool they can borrow or hold, on the Tool Catalog screen, and what state each one is in: available, checked out (and until when), reserved for the hold queue, or set aside for a holder. It is the neighbors' working screen for tools: they check tools out and place holds from it.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening the Tool Catalog screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool that is in the shed or out on loan and not retired, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Every neighbor sees exactly the same catalog (INV-TCAT-5). Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Check Out (Check Out Tool slice) — offered by the tool's state alone (INV-TCAT-11).
    • Place Hold (Place Hold slice) — offered by the tool's state alone (INV-TCAT-7).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Catalog built from events: "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Hold Placed", "Hold Cancelled", "Tool Returned", "Hold Fulfilled", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Catalog screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because Check Out Tool and Place Hold each check their own rules when they run.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, LoanId, HoldId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

FieldTypeSource / Notes
toolIdToolIdTool Added.toolId.
nameTextTool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
descriptionTextOptional. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDaysIntTool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays: whole days, 1–30.
addedAtInstantTool Added.addedAt.
statusTextOne of available, checked-out, reserved, set-aside. Derived: see the status rules below.
dueDateDateOptional. Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while status is checked out; none otherwise.
holdsWaitingIntDerived: the number of this tool's holds that have been placed and have neither been fulfilled nor ended.
canCheckOutBoolDerived: yes unless status is checked out (INV-TCAT-11).
canPlaceHoldBoolDerived: yes unless status is available (INV-TCAT-7).

Status rules. A tool's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. checked-out — a loan of the tool is open: Tool Checked Out has been recorded, and neither Tool Returned nor Tool Lost for that loan.
  2. set-aside — otherwise, a hold on the tool has been fulfilled and has not yet ended.
  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when Hold Cancelled, Hold Expired or Hold Collected is recorded for it; retiring the tool, recording it lost and closing the holder's account each record Hold Cancelled for the holds they end. Because the test reads current facts, the order events arrive in doesn't matter. For example, a lapsed set-aside whose tool has already gone out to someone else is checked-out, even before its Hold Expired lands.

To match later events to a tool, the view also keeps, for each tool, the loan ID of the current loan and the hold ID and holder of each live hold. These are bookkeeping, not part of the row, and are never returned.

Queries

  • List the catalog. Takes nothing; it is the same for every neighbor (INV-TCAT-5). Returns every listed tool, each with toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt, status, dueDate, holdsWaiting, canCheckOut and canPlaceHold. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool, ordered by name, then by addedAt (INV-TCAT-13).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TCAT-1: Every added tool appears in the catalog exactly once, available to borrow.
    • One entry per Tool Added. Nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each entry shows the tool's name, its description if it has one, and its default checkout period. Tools may share a name; each is its own entry.
    • A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added.
  • INV-TCAT-2: A checked-out tool shows as checked out, with its due date, until it is returned.
    • When the loan is extended, the catalog shows the new due date.
    • The due date is cleared when the tool comes back.
  • INV-TCAT-3: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, but not yet set aside, shows as reserved, never as available.
    • This covers the moment after a return before Hold Fulfilled lands, and the moment after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The catalog doesn't show who it is reserved for. Only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool enforces that (INV-CHK-3a).
  • INV-TCAT-4: A tool set aside for a holder shows as set aside until that holder checks it out or the set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside runs through the end of its collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days, and lapses at the start of the next day, shed local time. It also ends early if the holder cancels the hold or closes their account.
    • The catalog shows the set-aside until Hold Expired is recorded. The holder's claim ends at the cut-off even if that is a little earlier; Check Out Tool enforces it (INV-CHK-3b).
    • However it ends, other than by the holder's checkout, the tool's status follows the status rules: checked-out if someone else already has it out, else reserved if another hold is waiting, else available.
  • INV-TCAT-5: The catalog is the same for every neighbor.
    • It never shows a neighbor that a tool is set aside for them; they see their own set-aside on My Holds.
    • It never shows who a tool is checked out to, who holds it, or who it is reserved or set aside for. Only the shed manager sees borrowers, on the Tool Inventory.
  • INV-TCAT-6: Each tool shows how many holds are waiting on it.
    • A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends.
  • INV-TCAT-7: The catalog offers Place Hold on any tool that isn't available: checked out, reserved, or set aside.
    • A neighbor who wants an available tool checks it out instead.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone. A neighbor who can't place the hold (they already hold the tool, have it on loan, or are suspended) still sees it, and Place Hold refuses them with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-8: A retired tool drops off the catalog at once, including one retired while on loan.
    • Retiring a tool also ends its holds.
    • This differs from the Tool Inventory, which keeps a tool retired while on loan until it comes back or is recorded lost (INV-TINV-2). Neighbors can do nothing with a retired tool; the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TCAT-9: Only Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Tool Returned, Hold Fulfilled, Hold Collected, Hold Expired, Tool Retired and Tool Lost change the catalog.
    • Overdue notices, pickup emails and email changes are shown elsewhere, not here.
  • INV-TCAT-10: A tool recorded lost drops off the catalog.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires it and ends its holds, all at once.
  • INV-TCAT-11: The catalog offers Check Out on an available, reserved or set-aside tool. It doesn't offer Check Out on a tool that is checked out.
    • The action is offered by the tool's state alone, the same to every neighbor. On a reserved or set-aside tool, only the holder whose turn it is can check it out; Check Out Tool refuses anyone else with the reason.
  • INV-TCAT-13: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-TCAT-12: Applying the same event twice leaves the catalog as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TCAT-14: Any signed-in neighbor can read the Tool Catalog; a caller with no sign-in can't.
    • A caller with no sign-in is refused with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TCAT-1, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a 7-day default checkout period
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill, its description and its 7-day period, as available, with no holds waiting, Check Out offered and Place Hold not offered.
  • Two identical tools (INV-TCAT-1)
    • Given: the catalog lists one tool named "Cordless drill"
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second tool named "Cordless drill", with its own tool ID
    • Then: the catalog lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TCAT-12)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: the same Tool Added, and the same Hold Placed, for the drill are applied again
    • Then: the catalog still lists the drill once, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with Place Hold offered and Check Out not offered. It doesn't show who borrowed it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for the drill's loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October.
  • Hold placed (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Hold cancelled while the tool is out (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for one of those holds
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Tool returned, no holds waiting (INV-TCAT-2)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 19 October, with no holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no due date.
  • Tool returned, holds waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-7, INV-TCAT-11)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with no due date and 2 holds waiting, and offers both Check Out and Place Hold on it.
  • Only waiting hold cancelled while reserved (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for that hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available, with no holds waiting.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-TCAT-4, INV-TCAT-5, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for the drill's front hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting, and offers Check Out and Place Hold on it. Every neighbor sees the same entry, including the holder it is set aside for.
  • Holder collects the set-aside tool (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder, due 24 October
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 2 holds waiting
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by the holder at the front of the queue, due 24 October
    • Then: that holder's hold ends. The catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 24 October, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside expires, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting. Once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for that hold, it shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting.
  • Lapsed set-aside taken by someone else before the expiry lands (INV-TCAT-2, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, with Cara's hold waiting. Ben's collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired has not been recorded.
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill by Cara, due 25 October, and then Hold Expired is recorded for Ben's hold
    • Then: after the checkout, the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October, with no holds waiting. After the expiry, it still shows the drill as checked out, due 25 October. It never shows the drill as available or reserved.
  • Set-aside expires, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with no holds waiting
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Set-aside hold cancelled, another hold waiting (INV-TCAT-3, INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for the set-aside hold
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill as reserved, with 1 hold waiting.
  • Set-aside holder closes their account, no hold waiting (INV-TCAT-4)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as set aside for Cara, with no holds waiting
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for Cara's hold
    • Then: the catalog lists the drill as available.
  • Waiting holder closes their account (INV-TCAT-6)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, with 2 holds waiting, one of them Cara's, and the hedge trimmer as checked out with 1 hold waiting, Cara's
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for each of Cara's two holds
    • Then: the catalog shows the drill with 1 hold waiting and the hedge trimmer with none. Both are still checked out.
  • Tool retired in the shed (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill as available, and the ladder as available
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the drill
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. The ladder is unchanged.
  • Tool retired while on loan (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the catalog shows the hedge trimmer as checked out, due 20 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the catalog at once, though its loan carries on.
  • Retired tool's later events change nothing (INV-TCAT-8)
    • Given: the hedge trimmer was retired while on loan and has dropped off the catalog
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for its loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer does not come back into the catalog.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TCAT-10)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October, with 1 hold waiting
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill drops off the catalog. Other tools are unchanged.
  • Events the catalog doesn't hear (INV-TCAT-9)
    • Given: the catalog shows the drill as checked out, due 12 October
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for the drill's loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing order (INV-TCAT-13)
    • Given: the catalog lists a ladder, then a cordless drill added on 1 October, then a second cordless drill added on 3 October
    • When: a neighbor lists the catalog
    • Then: the tools come back as: the cordless drill added 1 October, the cordless drill added 3 October, then the ladder.
  • Listing the catalog (INV-TCAT-5)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill (checked out, due 12 October, 1 hold waiting) and the ladder (available)
    • When: Ana lists the catalog, and then Ben does
    • Then: both get the same two tools with the same fields, with no paging, and nothing about who has borrowed or holds either tool.
  • No sign-in (INV-TCAT-14)
    • Given: the catalog lists the drill
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the catalog
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TCAT-12). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: once a tool has been retired or recorded lost, its later events (a Tool Returned for a loan that carried on after retirement, or a replay) change nothing.
  • Hold events for a tool that is no longer listed: a hold can't be placed on a retired tool, and retirement ends its holds, so a hold event for an unlisted tool can only be a replay. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Check Out on a tool someone else has just borrowed). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Catalog is the neighbors' screen, for any signed-in neighbor; sign-in is handled outside the shed's events. It shows only tool details and state, the same to everyone.
  • PII & compliance: none. The catalog shows no neighbor's name, email or identity. The holders and borrowers it keeps for matching events are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • Tool Added and the loan events' keys match slices/add-tool.md and slices/tool-inventory.md. The hold events are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Check Out Tool and Place Hold.

Open Questions

None.
